title: The five jobs
worth automating
first in a small
business
slides.subtitle: Not the chatbot. Start with the money that leaks quietly, every week, without anyone noticing.

slides.label: Answering the phone you miss
slides.detail: Every missed call is a job somebody else quoted for. It never appears on a report and never gets blamed for anything, which is exactly why it survives for years.
slides.start: Where your calls actually go after five rings. Ring it yourself at 4pm on a Friday.

slides.label: Turning a job into a quote
slides.detail: Notes and photos in, a priced document out. The gap between visiting a job and sending the number is where warm work goes cold, and it is usually measured in days.
slides.start: Your last ten quotes. How many hours between the visit and hitting send?

slides.label: Chasing the invoice
slides.detail: Polite, on time, every time, without you having to decide to do it. A lot of what gets called a cash flow problem is really a chasing problem wearing a disguise.
slides.start: How many days past due your average paid invoice actually was.

slides.label: The follow-up nobody does
slides.detail: You have already done the expensive part. You visited, you priced it, you wrote it up. A quote that is never chased once is the cheapest revenue in the building.
slides.start: Quotes you sent more than fourteen days ago that nobody ever replied to.

slides.label: Writing the same reply again
slides.detail: If you have typed it twenty times, it should not need typing a twenty-first. Most inboxes have about five questions on permanent repeat and everyone answers them from scratch.
slides.start: Your sent folder. Find the five things you keep explaining.

title: Pick one.
Not five.
slides.body: The businesses that get real value out of this are the ones that fixed a single process properly and left everything else alone until it was genuinely working. Doing all five at once is how you end up with five half-built things and no time back.
slides.cta: Which of these is costing you most right now, the phone or the paperwork?
